legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Emu: Generative Pretraining in Multimodality", Quan Sun, Qiying Yu, Yufeng Cui, Fan Zhang, Xiaosong Zhang, Yueze Wang, Hongcheng Gao, Jingjing Liu, Tiejun Huang, Xinlong Wang (BAAI, Tsinghua, Peking U). ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2307.05222v2, May 2024). Note: the PDF is v2/ICLR; it cites DreamLLM (Sep 2023) and CM3Leon, so those rows are post-v1.

COVERAGE: All 29 pages, 91,342 of 91,342 chars (main text, ethics, appendices A-E, Tables 5-11, qualitative figures). References were skimmed. Extraction was clean. No embedded instructions found.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Core design. Images are encoded by EVA-CLIP, compressed by a Causal Transformer into N fixed visual embeddings, and interleaved with text tokens in a 14B LLaMA-13B-based model. Text tokens get cross-entropy loss and visual embeddings get l2 regression, in one autoregressive objective.
  number: 14B params
  setup: EVA-01-CLIP 1B encoder, LLaMA-13B, Causal Transformer of 12 blocks (random init), Stable Diffusion v1.5 decoder; images 224x224
  quote: "We adopt the cross-entropy classification loss for discrete text tokens, and the ℓ2 regression loss for continuous visual embeddings." / "The total number of parameters of Emu is 14B and is trained end-to-end."
  where: p3, p6
- claim: Rationale for the Causal Transformer. Raster-order autoregression over pixels or patches is poor, so 2D features are turned into a 1D causal latent sequence. No ablation of this choice is reported.
  number: none
  setup: each block has causal self-attention, cross-attention to EVA-CLIP features (keys/values), and an FFN
  quote: "Auto-regressively modeling images in raster order is counter-intuitive and has not demonstrated satisfactory performance"
  where: p4
- claim: Image generation works by appending [IMG] and autoregressively producing N embeddings. A separately fine-tuned diffusion decoder turns them into pixels. It is a two-stage design: the LLM regresses embeddings, then SD decodes them.
  number: none
  setup: the decoder is trained after pretraining with the encoder, LLM and VAE frozen. Only the U-Net is updated.
  quote: "If the desired output is image, we will append a [IMG] token at the end of the input sequence, then Emu will autoregressively generate N visual embeddings that will then be sent to the visual decoder"
  where: p5-6
- claim: Pretraining scale and cost are modest.
  number: 128 A100-80G, 10k steps, ~82M samples, 150B tokens, ~2 days
  setup: data are LAION-2B, LAION-COCO, MMC4, WebVid-10M and YT-Storyboard-1B. Batch sizes are 128/64/16/16 per source (Table 5 lists 128, 128, 64, 16, 16).
  quote: "We train the model on 128 NVIDIA 80G-A100 GPUs for 10k steps with around 82M samples (150B tokens in total), and the pretraining takes approximately 2 days."
  where: p6
- claim: Video as interleaved data. YT-Storyboard-1B pairs YouTube storyboard thumbnails with subtitles by timestamp. Using thumbnails avoids video decoding and cuts storage about 20x.
  number: 18M videos, 1.8B images, 20x storage reduction
  setup: video IDs from YT-Temporal-1B. 8 frames are sampled per video in pretraining.
  quote: "this approach leads to a substantial 20-fold reduction in data storage costs, resulting in increased download efficiency."
  where: p5, p16
- claim: Ablation shows YT-Storyboard-1B helps modestly. COCO CIDEr rose 110.8 to 112.9, MSVDQA k=4 rose 31.1 to 34.9, and OKVQA zero-shot with text-only examples (k=0*) fell 43.9 to 42.3.
  number: see claim
  setup: small Emu-7B (EVA-CLIP-Large + LLaMA-7B), 7.2k steps plus 2.4k extra on storyboard data. Single run, no variance reported.
  quote: "Emu-7B w/o YT-Storyboard-1B 110.8 43.9 44.6 30.2 31.1 16.9 19.9 / Emu-7B w/ YT-Storyboard-1B 112.9 42.3 45.7 30.8 34.9 17.9 20.8"
  where: p17 (Table 6)
- claim: Zero-shot understanding. Emu gets COCO CIDEr 112.4. Instruction-tuned Emu-I gets 120.4, and 14B Emu-I beats Flamingo-80B on some tasks.
  number: CIDEr 112.4 / 120.4; VQAv2 62.0 vs 56.3; VizWiz 38.3 vs 31.6; MSVDQA 37.0 vs 35.6
  setup: zero-shot. Emu uses multimodal chain-of-thought (caption first, then answer). The * rows use two text-only examples with the images removed. The 62.0 / 38.3 / 37.0 figures are Emu-I* rows. Emu-I trails Emu on VizWiz (32.2 vs 34.2), VisDial and NExTQA (5.8 vs 19.6) without *.
  quote: "Emu-I can outperform much larger-scale Flamingo-80B model in several tasks such as VQAv2 (62.0% vs. 56.3%), VizWiz (38.3% vs. 31.6%), and MSVDQA (37.0% vs. 35.6%)."
  where: p7 (Table 1)
- claim: Emu loses to dedicated image generators on FID, though it beats GILL, the other LLM-based generator.
  number: FID 11.66 (Emu) vs 12.20 (GILL) vs 9.93 (SDv1.5) vs 7.27 (Imagen) vs 7.23 (Parti)
  setup: zero-shot, 30k random MS-COCO val prompts, PNDM scheduler, 50 steps, classifier-free guidance scale 5.0 (Emu) and 3.0 (SD1.5)
  quote: "However, our model is inferior to SDv1.5 in terms of FID. This is probably because the condition space (image embeddings) of our visual decoder deviates a lot from the condition space (text embeddings) of the diffusion model used as initialization, and our model is trained for a relatively short 15k steps."
  where: p7-8 (Table 2)
- claim: Few-shot in-context performance rises with k and beats Flamingo-9B and Kosmos-1.
  number: Emu 4-shot VQAv2 58.4, VizWiz 41.3, MSRVTTQA 21.8; Flamingo-9B 56.3 / 34.9 / 18.2
  setup: k=2,4,8, RICES retrieval of examples by EVA-CLIP cosine similarity. 5000 random train samples per dataset. Video queries use 8 frames, support videos 2 frames.
  quote: "Emu achieves a VQAv2 accuracy of 58.4% and VizWiz 41.3% under the 4-shot setting, surpassing Flamingo-9B by +2.1% and +6.4%, respectively."
  where: p8 (Table 3), p20
- claim: MM-Vet in-the-wild score is 36.3 for Emu-I-14B, ahead of LLaVA-65B at 35.5. It is weak on Math (3.8) and Spat (25.2).
  number: 36.3 ±0.3 total
  setup: zero-shot, mean and std over 5 runs. The margin over DreamLLM-7B (35.9) is within roughly two stds.
  quote: "Emu-I -14B 45.5 19.2 36.7 35.9 25.2 3.8 36.3±0.3"
  where: p8 (Table 4)
- claim: Instruction tuning is light. LoRA is applied only to the LLM's self-attention layers, and everything else is frozen. It takes about 16 hours.
  number: LoRA rank=alpha=16; 16 A100-80G, ~16 h; batch 128, 10K steps; LR 1e-5
  setup: data are ShareGPT (~70K), Alpaca (52K), LLaVA filtered 158K to 130K, VideoChat-11K and ~30K Video-ChatGPT. Loss is on the answer only.
  quote: "The overall instruction tuning stage takes around 16 hours with 16 A100-80G GPUs. We attach LoRAs (Hu et al., 2022) on all linear projections of the self-attention layer, with the LoRA rank and alpha being 16."
  where: p6, p18
- claim: Data-curation lessons. The detailed-description subset of LLaVA was dropped because it made the model produce instruction-irrelevant descriptions. Samples containing a degenerate phrase were filtered. WebVid metadata (resolution, camera parameters) was cleaned, and ~1M captions were rewritten with Vicuna-13B. MMC4 images were dropped below a CLIP-similarity threshold. Decoder training prompts over 150 length were dropped.
  number: CLIP threshold 0.32; ~1M WebVid captions cleaned; LLaVA 158K to 130K; length filter drops ~8% of LAION-Aesthetics and 0.01% of LAION-COCO
  setup: described in the appendix, with no ablations
  quote: "any image with a CLIP similarity score below the threshold of 0.32 for all text in the same document is discarded."
  where: p16, p18
- claim: Eval prompting tricks matter. Multimodal CoT (generate a caption first, then answer) is a test-time technique. VizWiz "unanswerable" is handled by a yes/no gate ("is the answer known?"). Text-only example prompts fix output format.
  number: none
  setup: prompt templates in Table 10 (e.g. "a picture of {caption}. based on the picture, {question} short answer:")
  quote: "The experimental results demonstrate that this test-time technique effectively improves the model's performance without any additional data, leveraging the inherent capability of the model itself."
  where: p20-21
- claim: Continuous embeddings (Emu) vs discrete image tokens (CM3Leon) vs AnyMAL.
  number: COCO captioning: Emu 112.4, AnyMAL-13B 99.5, CM3Leon 61.6. COCO FID: CM3Leon 10.82 vs Emu 11.66. VQAv2: 52.0 / 59.6 / 47.6 (AnyMAL ahead on VQAv2 and Emu behind it).
  setup: zero-shot, Table 11. The paper says Emu is SOTA on 5 of 6 columns, but CM3Leon's FID is better.
  quote: "CM3Leon discretizes images, but we directly input and output image continuous features. We can find that CM3Leon performs much worse than Emu on image-to-text tasks."
  where: p20-21 (Table 11)
- claim: Emu-I did not beat prior work on every benchmark. In Table 1, PaLI-X-55B (finetuned) is far ahead on COCO (149.2) and VQAv2 (86.0). Emu-I VQAv2 is 57.2 (62.0*). Emu is also below Flamingo-9B* on MSVDQA/MSRVTTQA/NExTQA zero-shot in the plain rows (18.8/8.3/19.6 vs 30.2/13.7/23.0).
  number: see claim
  setup: Table 1
  quote: "Flamingo-9B * 79.4 - 61.5 51.8 44.7 28.8 48.0 30.2 13.7 23.0" and "Emu 112.4 96.5 72.0 52.0 38.2 34.2 47.4 18.8 8.3 19.6"
  where: p7

LIMITS
- Authors concede: hallucination (visual and language), slow autoregressive inference, knowledge frozen after pretraining, possible non-factual output, English-centric ("proficiency in languages other than English is currently delicate"). Ethics section says it is research-only and that deployment needs risk analysis. Web data may contain personal images.
- Not shown: no ablation of Causal Transformer vs alternatives, of regression vs discrete tokens, or of N. The value of N is never stated in the text I read. No latency or throughput numbers, no human eval of generation, no hallucination benchmark, and no OCR or high-resolution evaluation (224x224 input, OCR 19.2 on MM-Vet). The image generation is weaker than plain SD1.5 and the decoder is trained only 15k steps. Quality of generation is shown only via cherry-picked qualitative figures. The ablation uses a 7B model, single runs, and has one mixed result.
- Dated: LLaMA-1 base, SD1.5, CLIP-style 224px encoder, the benchmarks and baselines (Flamingo, Kosmos-1, BLIP-2, LLaVA-65B, MiniGPT-4) are mid-2023. Later unified models are not covered.

BUILDS ON: Flamingo (Alayrac et al., 2022; interleaved data, few-shot, RICES via Yang et al., 2022b), EVA-CLIP (Sun et al., 2023), LLaMA (Touvron et al., 2023), Stable Diffusion (Rombach et al., 2022), Kosmos-1 (Huang et al., 2023, multimodal CoT prompting), MMC4 (Zhu et al., 2023b), OpenFlamingo (Awadalla et al., 2023; CLIP filter), YT-Temporal-1B (Zellers et al., 2022), LLaVA (Liu et al., 2023b), LoRA (Hu et al., 2022), classifier-free guidance (Ho & Salimans, 2022), GILL (Koh et al., 2023a, concurrent), BLIP-2 Q-Former (Li et al., 2023b), "Language models are general-purpose interfaces" (Hao et al., 2022).

CODE: none (no code in the paper). Useful verbatim templates:
- Instruction packing (p7, eq. 2): "<System Message> [USER]: <Instruction> [ASSISTANT]: <Answer>" (only the Answer is in the loss; [USER]/[ASSISTANT] special tokens are initialised from the embeddings of "user"/"assistant")
- Emu image QA prompt (p21, Table 10): "a picture of {caption}. based on the picture, {question} short answer:"
- Image system message (p19, Table 8): "You are a helpful assistant and you will be presented with an image: [IMG]ImageContent[/IMG]. You will be able to see the image after I provide it to you. Please answer my questions based on the given image."

FIGURES
- Fig 2 (p4): "Emu unifies the modeling of different modalities in an auto-regressive manner..." Architecture diagram: encoder, causal transformer, LLM with classification or regression heads, and decoder. Best single figure for the notes.
- Fig 3 (p6): interleaved video-text data from storyboard thumbnails plus timestamped subtitles. Shows how video becomes interleaved data.
- Fig 1 (p2): generalist interface examples (captioning, VQA, in-context text-to-image, image blending).
- Fig 8/9 (p25-26): in-context text-to-image with and without context, showing style carried over.
- Fig 10-12 (p27-29): qualitative comparisons with LLaVA, mPLUG-Owl, InstructBLIP and Video-ChatGPT. These are single cherry-picked examples. Fig 11 shows Emu listing 8 Agatha Christie books while the baselines did not.
- Tables worth reproducing: Table 1 (zero-shot), 2 (FID), 3 (few-shot), 6 (video ablation), 11 (vs CM3Leon/AnyMAL).

PROBLEMS: None with extraction beyond the two-column layout interleaving table headers (e.g. Table 3's PALI-X row is incomplete in the text: "PALI-X - 56.9 57.1" with no column labels, so its k-columns are ambiguous). Table 3 text order is jumbled with Table 2, but the numbers quoted above were read from rows. Page numbers are PDF pages, which match the printed numbers.
